title: A dead man fooled Hitler

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: In 1943, a dead man fooled Hitler.
beats.visual: A coffin-shaped briefcase drifts toward camera on sketched waves; Hitler silhouette turns to look

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Britain needed Germany to ignore Sicily.
beats.visual: Sketch map of the Mediterranean; Sicily glows, a big arrow is hidden under a sheet

beats.speaker: q
beats.visual: Ava icon; question mark over a mortuary tag

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Glyndwr Michael, a homeless Welshman killed by rat poison, renamed Major William Martin. But there was a problem.
beats.visual: PD 1943 photo of Glyndwr Michael slides in from the edge; ID card 'Major W. Martin, Royal Marines' stamps over it

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: How do you fake an officer?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: With props: a fiancée's photo, theatre tickets, a ring receipt. A submarine released him off Spain, carrying a letter pointing at Greece.
beats.visual: Pocket items pop out one by one; PD photo of HMS Seraph officers; sketch map pin at Huelva; letter with arrow to Greece

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Exactly. German agents copied the letter. Hitler sent tanks to Greece. In July 1943, the Allies hit Sicily.
beats.visual: Letter photocopied by a sketched spy; tank token slides France to Greece on map; landing arrows hit Sicily

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: His Huelva grave now bears his real name.
beats.visual: Sketch of the Huelva headstone; second line of text writes itself in

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: A dead nobody fooled Hitler. Follow History Sketches for one wild true story every day.
beats.visual: Briefcase snaps shut; History Sketches corner logo

cta: Follow History Sketches for one wild true story every day.
description: In 1943 British intelligence dressed the body of Glyndwr Michael, a homeless Welshman, as a fake Royal Marines officer and let it wash up in Spain carrying false invasion plans. Hitler moved troops to Greece; the Allies landed on Sicily. Narration: synthetic voices. Facts checked against two sources. #history #shorts #ww2 #operationmincemeat
